$comment: The news module's register. news/tools/poll.py reads this file; news/AGENTS.md explains the fields. An id here is also the prefix of the source id a page cites.

feeds.note: The 'san-francisco' feed carries the whole Bay Area; the item's <category> tags are the real filter — one item is tagged San Jose, Oakland, Bay Area and San Francisco at once. No archive route: sitemap.xml answers 403, like its article pages, and ?paged=N returns page 1. The feed is the only way in, so a run that misses two days loses those stories for good.
Mission-district focused, and the densest address source of the set: street numbers reach the headline often.

backfill.note: ?paged=N on the feed. Measured 2026-09-12: pages cleanly, ~10 items a page at about six stories a day, so a month of the archive is roughly twenty pages plus the pages published since it. The end of the archive arrives as a 404.

feeds.note: Openings and closings — address-rich, but the 'san-francisco' edition files stories from Guerneville, Oakland and the Peninsula under the same feed. Trailing slash matters: without it the request 301s. No archive route found: ?paged=N 404s and the site publishes no sitemap we can read. A going-forward source.

NOT POLLED. rss.bizjournals.com/robots.txt ends with a blanket 'User-agent: * / Disallow: /' after the Cloudflare-managed group that allows it, and names ClaudeBot among the crawlers it disallows. research/AGENTS.md says a source that forbids automated access is a needs-human question, not a workaround. Left registered so the decision is visible; set access to 'open' to poll it.

Posts, not articles: no <title> at all, the headline has to come out of the post text, and the article URL is the last link in it — often a bit.ly. The account posts national and Hawaii weather stories too.

backfill.note: app.bsky.feed.getAuthorFeed, unauthenticated, 100 posts a call with a cursor. Its ids are the same at:// URIs the RSS view uses as <guid>, so both routes share one cursor. The API also states the article's real URL, which the post text does not — this account posts bit.ly links — and carries the outlet's own headline in the link card. About thirty posts a day, so a month is nine or ten calls.

feeds.note: Same shape as the Chronicle account. Its links are sfexaminer.com articles with utm_ parameters — strip them before citing. Overlaps sf-examiner; the cursor pair keeps one article from being read twice.

backfill.note: Same route as the Chronicle account. Overlaps sf-examiner's own archive, and the two cursors are what keep one article from being read twice; the sitemap route is the fuller of the two.

feeds.note: Commercial real estate across Northern California — sales, leases and development, so a high address rate on the items that are actually in the city. Its <category> tags name the county or city.

backfill.note: ?paged=N on the feed, ~10 items a page. It also publishes sitemap_index.xml, but the Yoast child sitemaps are not named by date, so a window cannot be chosen before fetching them and the paged walk is the cheaper route.

feeds.note: Covers Oakland and the wider region under the same feed. Its sitemap.xml indexes sitemap-posts.xml, a single 17MB document of 50,000 URLs with the publication date in each path — a workable archive route, but one that costs the whole file per window, so it is measured and not yet wired. ?paged=N is ignored and returns page 1.
robots.txt allows '*' and blocks named AI crawlers (ClaudeBot, GPTBot). We poll the feed it publishes for readers, identify ourselves, and link back.

backfill.note: 71 monthly sitemaps back to 2021-01, one request a month: 294 URLs for August 2026. They carry no titles, so the screen reads a headline reconstructed from the slug and the reading stage takes the real one off the article. The publication date is in the path (/2026/08/31/slug/); <lastmod> is the nightly rebuild and says nothing. ?paged=N is ignored by this feed and returns page 1.

feeds.note: A section page, not a feed: no dates and no summaries, so the cursor is the set of article URLs seen. robots.txt allows '*' on /news/ and disallows named AI crawlers by name.

backfill.note: A TownNews site: one index per year of per-day sitemaps, and robots.txt lists the years back to 1900. A day is one request of about five URLs. No titles and no date in the path, so the headline is reconstructed from the slug and the date comes from <lastmod>, which here is the publication timestamp.

feeds.note: Development only — proposals, permit filings, hearings, site visits — so nearly every item is a building story. Its first <category> is the street address itself ('38 8th Street', '262 7th Street') and the rest name the architect, developer and contractor; that tag is why an item screens as an address even when the headline names only a neighborhood, and the named firms are the ones the root AGENTS.md allows a page to credit. 'The San Francisco metropolitan region' reaches San Jose and Sacramento, but the headline always ends with the city ('…, San Jose'), so the screen skips those on the headline rule. Only five items deep: a run that misses two days loses stories.

backfill.note: ?paged=N on the feed, five items a page, ending between paged=800 (December 2021) and paged=1200. The highest-yield backfill target in the register: development-only, the first <category> is the street address itself, and the rest name the architect, developer and contractor.

feeds.note: A city-only newsroom launched April 2024; its sections run Housing, Business, Neighborhoods and Crime alongside Opinion, A&E, Events and poetry. The feed syndicates the entire article in both <description> and content:encoded, so the screen reads a whole body rather than a summary and some story shape matches almost every item — a family-film column queued on 'school'. It over-queues by design rather than by fault; expect to decline several per run at the read stage. Ten items deep.

backfill.note: ?paged=N on the feed, ten items a page; paged=110 is 12 April 2024, its launch, so the archive is complete at about 1,100 items. It syndicates whole articles, so the screen reads a body rather than a summary and over-queues by design.
